A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Towards Fair In-Context Learning with Tabular Foundation Models. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification and fairness results, sensitive-attribute reconstruction experiments, and context-size and correlation-removal analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds runtime measurements, ROC-AUC comparisons, and a TabICL context-size ablation.

M1.justification: The three preprocessing interventions, uncertainty-estimation variants, and foundation models remain unchanged. Selecting samples with two-label conformal prediction sets was already specified in v3. The training-only correlation-removal variant S2 also already appeared in v3 Section 4.5.

E1.justification: The named datasets and tasks, including the Adult comparison, remain unchanged. However, v3 Appendix A additionally reports experiments on other ACS states; v4 removes that footnote. This modestly narrows documented geographic coverage without establishing that those experiments ceased.

E2.justification: Group Balanced is added to the corresponding fairness–utility comparisons, including v4 Figure 1 and Figures 7–10. Although this method already appeared elsewhere as Balanced, it was absent from these Pareto comparisons in v3. The Adult comparison methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 replaces five-fold cross-validation on the data remaining after the sensitive-classifier holdout with an 80/20 training/test split of that remainder. This substantially changes the reported evaluation design. v4 also introduces supplementary ROC-AUC evaluation and wall-clock timing protocols.

E4.justification: v4 adds computational-cost comparisons across models and interventions on CelebA and ACSIncome, checks tradeoffs using ROC-AUC in Figures 11–12, and extends context-size sensitivity analysis to TabICL in Figure 13. These substantially broaden supplementary validation; the existing TabPFN ablation and correlation-removal failure analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v3 specifies ten independent runs and mean/standard-deviation aggregation across five-fold test sets. v4 instead specifies three random seeds and omits the earlier main-result aggregation description. Its timing tables explicitly report standard deviations over three seeds. This substantially revises documented replication without establishing whether retained tables were recomputed.

E6.justification: v4 revises numerous Pareto-plot results, adds ROC-AUC and TabICL ablation results, and introduces runtime tables—for example, 10.71±1.27 seconds for vanilla TabPFN on CelebA. It removes v3's fixed-parameter benchmark results in Figure 1/Table 5. The Adult, reconstruction, and CR-variant tables retain their numbers. Changed protocol descriptions preclude treating revised curves as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix B retains Equations 1–14, including the fairness definitions, correlation-removal derivation, conformal prediction sets, and exchangeability assumption. The rewritten selection example restates existing mathematics rather than adding a formal result or changing the rule.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the first-investigation claim, three preprocessing approaches, and improved group fairness with limited accuracy cost and no foundation-model updates. The broader 'fairness–utility' terminology accommodates additional evidence without materially redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds a dataset-specific explanation contrasting nearly gender-balanced ACS data with race-imbalanced Diabetes, plus efficiency and deployment interpretations. It removes v3 Appendix C's explicit caveat that interventions on low-unfairness PublicCoverage and Diabetes settings can reduce accuracy without improving fairness, along with the associated parameter-selection discussion.

D1.justification: New Appendix C specifies the reported NVIDIA A100 hardware, memory, and operations included in timing measurements. The previous fixed epsilon=0.05 experimental specification disappears, although that value remains in explanatory examples. Code and library references remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds TabArena by Erickson et al. (2025) as supporting benchmark context and removes Kenfack et al. (2023), replacing its preprocessing citation with the already-cited Feldman et al. (2015). The positioning relative to LLM-based ICL and FairPFN remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main structure and much of the prose remain intact. Localized revisions reorganize Section 4.2 around tradeoffs and sensitive-attribute reconstruction, number the selection-method subsections, label research questions, and standardize utility terminology. v4 also introduces a runtime appendix and removes the acknowledgements.

P2.justification: The evidence presentation is substantially reorganized: the reconstruction table moves into the main text, ACSTravelTime panels appear in main figures, appendix plots are consolidated, and Pareto axes and legends are revised. The bar chart and fixed-setting table disappear, while two timing tables and three additional analysis figures are introduced.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful runtime, ROC-AUC, and TabICL robustness evidence. However, it removes exact fixed-setting results and a substantive failure caveat, while reducing stated replication without explaining how unchanged tables relate to the revised protocol. Its new claim that Uncertain+LR is consistently fastest also conflicts with Table 5: TabDPT takes 595.58 seconds with Uncertain+LR versus 316.86 with Uncertain+TabPFN. These evidential gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
